review.summary: Round 2 re-reviews the whole TASK-069D branch with a focus on the fix commit for the two round 1 findings, both of which are resolved. The fix commit changes only the two test modules; migrations, models and documentation are unchanged since round 1. The PostgreSQL test now rejects deleting a client that only a grant references, and a mutant with a cascading grant-to-client foreign key now fails that assertion, while the real schema passes. A new parametrised SQLite test rejects ten invalid rows, each on its intended constraint, and the PostgreSQL constraint test adds blank client_id, blank grant_key and token expiry cases that fail on their intended constraints. Ruff, pyright, the model tests, the PostgreSQL migration integration tests on postgres:18.6 and the full backend suite pass. No new findings.

prior_finding_dispositions.rationale: The cascade test commits the grant and its tokens before any authorization request exists and asserts that deleting the client raises a RestrictViolation. A mutant that changes only the grant's client foreign key to ON DELETE CASCADE now fails at that assertion, while the real migration passes.

A parametrised SQLite test covers the blank client_id, created_ip and grant_key checks, token and authorization request expiry, empty and over-long redirect URIs, both halves of the code consistency check and consumed time without a code, each rejected by its intended constraint; a separate test accepts the 2,048-character boundary. The PostgreSQL constraint test adds the dialect-specific non-blank checks and token expiry.
